blurb: Naturally spotted cat with green eyes, a scarab brow mark and great speed
description: The Egyptian Mau is a rare cat breed from Egypt, small to medium-sized and muscular, with a naturally spotted tabby coat, light green eyes and great speed.
answer: The Egyptian Mau is a rare, small to medium-sized cat breed associated with Egypt and one of the few naturally spotted domestic breeds. It is muscular, with longer hind legs, a spotted coat, a scarab-like forehead marking and light green eyes.

body: The modern breed began in 1953 in Italy, when Princess Natalie Trubetskoy obtained a female named Baba from Cairo with help from the Egyptian ambassador. Baba's descendants were first shown at the Rome Cat Show in 1955, and the princess took three Maus to the United States in 1956. The CFF granted championship in 1968, the CFA recognized the breed in 1977 and TICA in 1979. The first Maus reached Britain in 1998. Genetic studies place it among Western-derived breeds.

The Mau is described as balancing the compactness of a Burmese with the slim elegance of a Siamese. It is muscular, with a medium-length body, prominent shoulder blades and hind legs longer than the front, plus a loose flap of skin from flank to hind knee. The head is gently rounded with a scarab-like tabby mark on the forehead, the ears medium to large, and the large round eyes light green, though kittens may have amber eyes. The coat is ticked and spotted; accepted colors are silver, bronze and smoke.
The source material says little about personality. The breed is noted as the fastest domestic cat, clocked at more than 48 km/h, which suggests an athletic animal; individual temperament varies.
Sources give little specific care detail. Given its athletic build and speed, space and opportunities to run and play suit the breed, along with regular veterinary check-ups.

Conditions reported in the breed include urate urolithiasis (bladder stones), which occurs more often than in mixed-breed cats; one Canadian study found it in 14 of 17 Maus surveyed. The breed's gestation is also reported to be longer than usual, at about 73 days.

faq.q: Is the Egyptian Mau the fastest domestic cat?
faq.a: It is described as the fastest domestic cat breed, clocked at more than 48 km/h (30 mph), helped by its long hind legs and flank skin flap.

faq.q: Is the Egyptian Mau naturally spotted?
faq.a: Yes. It is one of the few naturally spotted tabby breeds of domestic cat.

faq.q: What colors does the Egyptian Mau come in?
faq.a: Accepted colors are silver spotted tabby, bronze spotted tabby and black smoke.
